messages:
mike_support: FYI — ACME (customer) opened a high-severity ticket: streaming SSE responses cut off mid-event, client reconnects and we see duplicate consumption/billing for the same logical request. They can repro consistently when the client is on a flaky corp-proxy. Raising to eng + billing. full logs below and repro steps they sent.

acme-cs: reproducer: curl against our streaming endpoint behind corp-proxy, client is a mobile SDK that stalls reading for ~6s occasionally then reconnects. Example we used:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?session=abc123" --no-buffer
```
We see output like: `data: { partial chunk }` then stream stops with no close event, sdk reconnects and receives the remainder as a fresh billing event (we were charged twice).

acme-cs: Relevant server log excerpt: 
[2025-08-14T18:12:02.312Z] session=abc123 write() -> EAGAIN (resource temporarily unavailable)
[2025-08-14T18:12:02.412Z] session=abc123 write queue 4.2MB > abort_threshold 4MB -> aborting stream, close_code=1006 reason=write_timeout
[2025-08-14T18:12:02.413Z] session=abc123 connection closed by server (force-abort)
[2025-08-14T18:12:02.414Z] session=abc123 new connection from 35.202.14.9 (reconnect) id=session=abc123-2
[2025-08-14T18:12:02.915Z] session=abc123-2 started new stream; billing_token=bill_zzzz

mike_support: Attachments: full request IDs: r_20250814_5501 / r_20250814_5502. Customer says they were billed for both `bill_zzzz` and previous token even though the first stream didn't finish client-side.

tao_sre: Do we have server-side dedupe on billing tokens for retried streams? My quick answer: we bill per active stream start (token minted on Accept), not on final completion, so reconnects can cause additional charge.

jess_billing: Confirmed — current pipeline issues invoiceable units when a stream session is accepted and assigned a token. We don't currently mark tokens as idempotent across reconnections. We can do a manual credit for the customer but we should evaluate longer-term fix (idempotency keys or bill-on-completion).

ingrid_eng: Looking at the write abort logic. We intentionally abort streams when outgoing socket write backlog exceeds abort threshold to protect other tenants. The abort path currently emits close_code=1006 and does not set a final event in the SSE payload. That leaves the client in an ambiguous state and their SDK reconnect logic treats that as a fresh call (and a new billing token).

ingrid_eng: Quick fix options:
- Emit a structured final event before abort (e.g., `data: {"_server_final":true, "status":"aborted"}`) so well-behaved clients can detect and not re-bill.
- Change billing to only charge on first non-empty token consumption or on explicit completion acknowledgement.
- Increase per-connection sndbuf/queue limits for dedicated hosts for customers behind flaky proxies.

tao_sre: For debugging, can we get tcpdump or proxy logs from the customer showing stalls? Also need kernel send buffer sizes and our cgroup limits for the worker that handled r_20250814_5501.

mike_support: ACME uploaded a pcap and the corp-proxy adds a silent pause of ~5–8s between packets, which lines up with the client stall window. They also included SDK logs:
```
[2025-08-14 18:12:02.400] SSEReader stalled: no bytes read for 5900ms
[2025-08-14 18:12:02.405] SSEReader reconnecting (backoff 200ms)
```
ACME says sdk reconnect code is aggressive and treats any reconnect as a new purchase.

jess_billing: I'll authorize an immediate one-off credit for the duplicate billing and work with finance. We need a policy doc for streaming idempotency.

ingrid_eng: Deployed a small change to the abort path on staging to emit a final event payload when aborting for write_timeout. Patch: send(`data: {"_server_final":true,"error":"write_timeout"}

`) then close. This may help well-behaved clients detect server-abort vs network drop. Deploying canary now to prod-slo hosts for 1h.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary-group=prod-slo-hosts image=redwood/streamd:20250814-abort-final-emit sha=abcd1234

tao_sre: While canary runs, ops action items: increase worker send-queue threshold from 4MB to 8MB on dedicated pools serving ACME, validate memory headroom, and add a metric for `stream_abort_write_timeout_count`.

mike_support: Customer asks for mitigation steps they can apply now: they can tune their SDK reconnect logic to not auto-charge on reconnect (treat reconnect attempts as resume with same token when possible) or implement a short jittered backoff to allow late packets through. Also we recommended increasing socket keepalive and switching corp-proxy to pass through larger TCP window.

acme-cs: Thanks — we did the SDK change to treat reconnection as resume and accepted the credit. We'll test again and report.

jess_billing: Credit issued: invoice INV-2025-ACME-0814 amount $0.00 (test credit) — placeholder logged; finance will do final adjustment.

ingrid_eng: Next steps captured in internal ticket: PROD-STREAM-892: (1) Make server emit final event on abort (prod rollout next week), (2) Evaluate billing on completion vs on accept (design doc), (3) Add dedupe token option for enterprise customers, (4) Short-term increase of write-queue threshold for affected hosts.

mike_support: Closing loop: ACME satisfied with workaround and credit. Leaving open for eng follow-up and billing policy. Thanks everyone. :tada:
